title: 'Not engaged in any negotiations': Iran rejects Trump's claim of US talks, says restarting dialogue 'not in our DNA'- Moneycontrol.com
summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry denied US President Trump's claim that talks with Washington are underway, saying Tehran is "not engaged in any negotiations" and that restarting dialogue is "not in our DNA." While US officials described a pause in military action as creating space for diplomacy, Iran insisted the lull does not amount to resumed negotiations and said the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.
content:
Iran on Monday rejected US President Donald Trump's assertion that negotiations between Washington and Tehran are underway, insisting that no talks are currently taking place and dismissing suggestions that it had sought to reopen diplomatic channels.

According to Iran's Foreign Ministry, the country is "not engaged in any negotiations with the United States." The ministry further said it was the United States, not Tehran, that had sought talks, adding that restarting negotiations was "not in our DNA," according to Tasnim.

The remarks came even as military strikes between the two countries remained on hold for a second straight day, fuelling speculation over possible diplomatic efforts.

Tehran's latest statement directly contradicted claims by the Trump administration that diplomatic engagement with Tehran was continuing following the recent suspension of hostilities. While Washington has signalled that negotiations are being given an opportunity to progress, Tehran maintained that there are no ongoing discussions with the United States and reiterated that its position had not changed.

Despite Iran's denial, senior US officials indicated that the current pause in military action was intended to create space for diplomacy. US Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told Fox News that President Donald Trump was allowing negotiations "a little bit of room" after diplomatic efforts gathered pace. "The President is giving talks some space. We remain locked and loaded, but he's going to give negotiations a little bit of room," Waltz said.

According to CNN, a US source said military operations were currently "on hold" and that regional allies had not reported any fresh Iranian attacks during the pause.

Iran also confirmed that it had halted its retaliatory military operations following the suspension of US strikes. However, the Foreign Ministry stressed that the pause in hostilities should not be interpreted as the resumption of negotiations, maintaining that no diplomatic engagement with Washington is currently taking place.

The Foreign Ministry also reaffirmed that there had been no change in the situation in the Strait of Hormuz. According to Tasnim, Tehran said the strategic waterway remains completely closed to all lanes, reiterating its earlier position despite the ongoing pause in military operations.

The contrasting messages from Washington and Tehran leave uncertainty over whether the current lull in fighting could eventually lead to formal diplomatic engagement or remain only a temporary suspension of military action. Observers say the coming days will be crucial to determine whether the pause evolves into a substantive diplomatic process or merely a short-term de-escalation.
